newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paribas sells Havas stake in shake-up.
newsitem.headline: Paribas sells Havas stake in shake-up.

text.p: French bank Paribas said on Friday it had sold its remaining 3.5 percent stake in media group Havas in the latest shake-up after Generale des Eaux became its biggest shareholder.
Paribas sold its remaining stake in the market and analysts are awaiting the arrival of a U.S. ally in the capital of the French group with Time-Warner most often cited.

Jean-Marie Messier, the expansive chairman of Generale des Eaux, is in New York on Friday as part of a tour of meetings with institutional investors aimed at making clear he aims to streamline and straighten things at Havas.

At Generale des Eaux there was no comment but a spokesman said: "Since the publication of the company's results, the chairman has organised roadshows, mainly in Switzerland, and he is currently in New York."
Havas recently announced that one of its managing directors, Jean-Francois Meaudre, would leave the group June 30.
"Paribas has left our capital entirely," Havas finance director Nicolas Duhamel told Reuters on Friday.
"We confirm that we have sold our stake in Havas on the market," a Paribas spokeswoman said on Friday, declining to give further details.
Among other Havas shareholders that could sell their stakes are Caisse des Depots et Consignations, which has a little less than three percent, and Audiofina of Luxembourg which has 4.3 percent.
Audiofina is a holding company which has a major stake in CLT-UFA and, in turn, is controlled by Belgian businessman Albert Frere.

The sale or not of the Audiofina stake depends on the wider strategic issue of whether Frere is going to decide to break his ties with the Generale des Eaux/Havas/Canal Plus camp and concentrate on the CLT-Ufa/Bertelsmann alliance, or the other way around.
Havas wants to be able to "liquify" its stake in CLMM, an unlisted joint venture with Frere which has a large stake in Audiofina.
Market rumours are that Time-Warner could enter the Havas capital and also buy the CGV (Cie Generale de Videocommunication) cable unit of Generale des Eaux.
A company source, however, said no such negotiations were currently underway.
Banking sources said that Societe Generale was preparing "the arrival of an American in the capital of a major French communications group. The deal will be announced next week."
A Societe Generale spokeswoman had no comment.

On March 28, during the general meetings of Havas and pay-televison group Canal Plus in which Havas is the biggest shareholder after obtaining Generale des Eaux's shares in exchange for a stake in itself, Havas head Pierre Dauzier confirmed that there were "contacts" but "no negotiations" about the arrival of a foreign partner in the capital of the group.

He told the shareholders that "the company could attract foreign, Anglo-Saxon, shareholders who want to have an active partnership on the markets in which we operate and make joint investments in future markets."
Havas shares were 1.31 percent higher at 402 francs at 1055 GMT while the CAC-40 blue-chip index was 0.04 percent higher.
